clue.text: Hull's high-rise is an excellent building

parts.note: super is an informal word for excellent
a structure is a building or other construction

explanation.surface: Someone in the city of Hull admires a fine tall block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the English city, but it is a ship's hull: the part of a vessel built above it is the high-rise here.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the decks and cabins rising above the main hull are its upper works.

clue.text: Reps not going round to the back door

indicators.note: letters going round are turned about and rearranged, so the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Sales reps avoid the front entrance and slip in at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges the letters of REPS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a historical term for a rear or side gate, often in a castle wall.

clue.text: Reportedly documents are for stylish establishment

indicators.note: reportedly tells us we want a word that is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: writs are legal documents

explanation.surface: Paperwork is said to be meant for a classy business.
explanation.walkthrough: WRITS spoken sounds like the name of the London hotel famous for luxury; 'are for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The hotel name has become a byword for elegance and luxury, as in 'putting on the ritz'.

clue.text: How long thin spill is getting smaller?

explanation.surface: A question about a long slender thing narrowing as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: A spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire; a taper is the same kind of thing, and such a thing grows thinner towards its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: First sense: a spill narrows to a point; second sense: becoming gradually narrower or less.

clue.text: Mischievous child found in ancient city church to start with

indicators.note: to start with places the city and church first, ahead of the final little word

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city of the crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster is discovered in an old city church.
explanation.walkthrough: UR and CH come first, as 'to start with' says, then IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, mischievous youngster, especially one roaming the streets.

clue.text: Cruelly losing a right in a devious way?

indicators.note: losing tells us to take something out of the word before it

parts.note: torturously means in a cruel, torturing manner
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone acts with cruelty when deprived of an entitlement, seemingly underhandedly.
explanation.walkthrough: One R drops out of TORTUROUSLY, as 'losing' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortuous means winding and, by extension, deceitful or not straightforward.

clue.text: Again presented in sketchy fashion?

parts.note: sketchy suggests vague or slapdash, but here it is literal: a picture sketched a second time

explanation.surface: Something shown once more, only rather roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'sketchy' is meant literally, as in drawing a sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sketched a second time has been pencilled out anew.

clue.text: Stressing that lackey is going round inside

indicators.note: going round means the lackey word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an underling is a lackey or subordinate
inside gives the short word in

explanation.surface: A servant is walking around indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' tells the lackey word to surround the little piece, which sits just before its final letter; 'that' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a line beneath words emphasises them, just as stressing does.

clue.text: One therefore takes the subject relating to chemical elements

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means therefore
a topic is a subject

explanation.surface: Someone reasons logically and settles on a theme about chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are forms of the same chemical element with different neutron counts.

clue.text: Element found on small radiator first

indicators.note: first puts the short form of radiator at the front, before the little word

parts.note: rad is a short informal form of radiator
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is discovered sitting on a little heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts RAD ahead of ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive gaseous chemical element.

clue.text: Not half sorry to give one

definitions.text: Not half sorry to give one

parts.words: Not half sorry to give one
parts.note: not half reads as a measure (only half) but means completely, and the one given is an expression of regret

explanation.surface: Someone is very sorry to have to hand something over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much', and here also says nothing is held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offered in complete contrition rather than partial regret.

clue.text: One exploiting heartless doorkeeper

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: an usher keeps a door in a court or theatre

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted porter takes advantage of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes H, the central letter of USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses others or something is exploiting them or it.

clue.text: Say clearly that it means jointed

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a word means having joints.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pronounce distinctly; as an adjective it means having joints or segments, like a lorry.

clue.text: A positive development

parts.note: sounds like good news, but a positive is a print made from a negative in a darkroom

explanation.surface: Some welcome good news.
explanation.walkthrough: In film photography, developing produces a negative, and printing from it makes a positive.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed picture from a camera is the end product of developing film.

clue.text: Wish for help with ordinary writing

parts.note: to long is to wish or yearn
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Someone wants assistance with everyday penmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing by hand in full, as opposed to shorthand or typing.

clue.text: Passage with a light ending?

parts.note: plays on the saying about light at the end of an underground passage

explanation.surface: A piece of writing with a cheerful conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a piece of text and 'light ending' a happy close; it is the proverbial light at the end of a long underground route.
explanation.definitionFit: A bored underground route, famous in the saying about light at its far end.

clue.text: State of the beetle

explanation.surface: Asking which American region a beetle belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Rockies, and the striped potato beetle named after it.

clue.text: Quickly look over page about Ronald

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to look at the next page
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to check a page about a man named Ronald fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for 'please turn over' is printed at a page's foot to tell readers to look at the next page; 'about' wraps it round the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for straight away, borrowed from Spanish and Italian.

clue.text: Jack, before ten, it appears, first on the lake

indicators.note: first puts the little word at the very front of the answer
before places the sailor ahead of the number

parts.note: taken as written
a jack tar is a sailor, so tar means sailor or jack
10 written in figures looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives ahead of ten o'clock, first on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it appears' says the number ten in figures is read by its look as two letters; 'first' and 'before' fix the order of the three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America bears this name.

clue.text: Rough who, say, left a gin cocktail

indicators.note: say means the word before is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word spoken gives the sound of its first three letters

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mix, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A drinker abandons a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes WHO sound like HOO; 'cocktail' rearranges A GIN to IGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a noun for a ruffian or thug, as in a gang of roughs.

clue.text: Some flowers or fish splash down

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a spacecraft lands at sea when it splashes down

explanation.surface: A choice between a bouquet and a fish hitting the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of blooms worn or hung as decoration.

clue.text: Surprisingly stout member included-the greatest

indicators.note: included means the member letter goes inside the scrambled word
surprisingly says the following word is turned into something unexpected

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly portly club member was counted among the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges STOUT to UTOST; 'included' places M within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost means of the highest or furthest degree, the most extreme.

clue.text: Eccentric got initial case

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball has his first lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges the ten letters of GOT INITIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal case is a lawsuit or proceeding in court.

clue.text: Nearly-new part of fibre diet

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: brand, as in brand-new, stands for new

explanation.surface: A second-hand item forms part of a healthy eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' trims BRAND (as in brand-new) to BRAN; the surface reads 'nearly-new' as a shop term for second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of cereal grain, eaten for roughage.

clue.text: Second person in Dieppe to have North American fish

parts.note: tu is French for you, the familiar second person, and Dieppe is a French port

explanation.surface: Another person in a French port is served an American fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, a familiar example of the class.

clue.text: Some cougar darted into Italian lake

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big cat leaps into a lake in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'into' in the definition, but the lake itself is the definition; 'into' is a link joining wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy, in the north.

clue.text: Our Clara becoming wise and prophetic

indicators.note: becoming means turning into, so the letters of the two words turn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman named Clara grows into a sage seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges OUR CLARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Like an oracle, giving wise and authoritative pronouncements or forecasts.

clue.text: Might one burn one's fingers on it when it's stolen?

definitions.text: Might one burn one's fingers on it when it's stolen?

parts.words: Might one burn one's fingers on it when it's stolen?
parts.note: hot is slang for stolen, so stolen goods are risky to deal in, like something scalding

explanation.surface: A question about the danger of grabbing something.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot is slang for stolen, and stolen goods are dangerous to handle; the phrase also means too risky to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for something too risky or controversial to deal with, as well as literally scalding.
